title: There Must Be a Rainbow
summary: A lovely story about hope: Jabulile's dream of helping people comes true after a terrible storm strikes the valley.
pages: In the heart of the Zulu kingdom lies a wonderful place called the Valley.

Here lived a little girl named Jabulile. Jabulile was always a happy girl. She was also curious, and full of questions about life.
Everything fascinated her.
Jabulile's father grew corn. Her mother was a teacher. They taught her to dream big dreams. Jabulile's biggest dream was to help people.
All the people of the village were Jabulile's friends, especially the elders. They told her about the wise men and wise women who once lived in the Valley. Jabulile wanted to be wise too.
One terrible day, clouds began to gather over the Valley. Everything grew dark and gray. A terrible storm swept over the land.
Mighty gusts of wind blew the roofs off the huts. All the animals were left without a home. It was a very sad day.

The villagers cried, "What will we do now?"
"All the crops are ruined!" cried the farmers.
"Our homes are gone!" said the elders.
It seemed that all hope was lost. But Jabulile remembered something her wise father had once told her.

Jabulile began to speak to the villagers. "The storm hurts us," she said, "only because of the way we choose to see it. If you look up, you'll see that the sun is shining again. It's a new day.
"After every storm there must be a rainbow!" she cried excitedly.
And just then, a magnificent rainbow appeared in the sky.
The villagers saw the rainbow and began to smile. It stood there like a promise that the storm was over.
The villagers rebuilt their homes. The farmers planted new crops. The grass grew greener than ever.
And once again there was hope and joy in the Valley.
